quizzes.title: Checkpoint 1 — Pages, Blocks, and Databases
quizzes.intro: Check when to use pages versus databases and how properties work.

questions.prompt: When should you prefer a database over a single standalone page?

options.text: When you will never create more than one related item
When you have many similar items you need to filter, sort, and review
When you want to disable headings forever
When Notion is offline only

questions.explanation: Databases shine for repeated structured items with shared properties and views.

wrongExplanations.a: A one-off document is usually a page.
wrongExplanations.c: Databases do not replace ordinary writing needs.
wrongExplanations.d: Online/offline constraints are not the decision rule here.

options.text: The basic unit of page content such as paragraphs, headings, lists, and embeds
A paid invoice only
A Git commit hash
A forced full-screen advertisement

questions.explanation: Pages are composed of blocks that can be rearranged and transformed.

wrongExplanations.b: Billing is unrelated to the block concept.
wrongExplanations.c: Commit hashes belong to Git, not Notion structure.
wrongExplanations.d: Blocks are content units, not ads.

questions.prompt: Why start with fewer database properties than you think you need?

options.text: Because Notion forbids more than two properties
Because every property is a maintenance obligation and unused fields become noise
Because filters cannot use properties
Because titles are optional in databases

questions.explanation: Lean schemas are easier to keep accurate and actually use.

wrongExplanations.a: You can add many properties; restraint is about judgment.
wrongExplanations.d: Title is a core required field for database items.

questions.prompt: What are the recommended layers for a maintainable workspace?

options.text: Only polished dashboards with no capture inbox
Inbox for quick capture, working systems for weekly use, and slower-changing reference docs
One infinite page with no structure at all
Separate Notion accounts for every paragraph

questions.explanation: Capture first, structure second, polish third keeps systems usable under real workload.

wrongExplanations.a: Skipping capture leads to abandoned decorative systems.
wrongExplanations.c: Zero structure does not scale for recurring work.
wrongExplanations.d: That would create chaos, not clarity.

questions.prompt: What is unique about a database item in Notion?

options.text: It can only store a title and nothing else
It is itself a page, so it can hold rich content beyond the row properties
It cannot be filtered
It permanently deletes related pages every hour

questions.explanation: Each item combines structured properties with a full page body for notes and details.

wrongExplanations.a: Items commonly include many properties plus page content.
wrongExplanations.c: Filtering is a primary database feature.
wrongExplanations.d: Nothing about items requires hourly deletion.

quizzes.title: Checkpoint 2 — Views, Templates, and Systems
quizzes.intro: Test views, templates, and practical work/study system design.

options.text: A saved window onto the same database with its own layout, filters, and sorts
A duplicate copy of every row stored separately forever
A password for the workspace
A type of image crop tool

questions.explanation: Views change presentation and focus while sharing the underlying data.

wrongExplanations.b: Views do not duplicate the whole database by default.
wrongExplanations.c: Access control is separate from views.
wrongExplanations.d: Views are database presentations, not image editors.

questions.prompt: Which view is often best for moving tasks across workflow stages?

options.text: Board (kanban-style) grouped by status
A random gallery of unrelated images only
A page with no database at all
An archived PDF printout

questions.explanation: Board views make status movement visual and tangible for task systems.

wrongExplanations.b: Galleries are better for visual cards, not stage movement.
wrongExplanations.c: Workflow stages need structured properties and views.
wrongExplanations.d: Printouts are static and hard to update.

options.text: A three-page form nobody finishes
A short structure that asks the questions you forget under pressure
A template with fifty mandatory empty properties
No headings and no prompts at all

questions.explanation: Templates reduce blank-page friction when they are short enough to use consistently.

wrongExplanations.c: Excess mandatory fields kill capture and completion.
wrongExplanations.d: A template needs useful prompts to help.

questions.prompt: When should you add relations between databases?

options.text: Immediately on day one for every page
When navigation pain is real and connecting items will reduce repeated hunting
Only after deleting all views
Never, because relations are decorative only

questions.explanation: Relations are powerful but add complexity; introduce them when they solve a repeated problem.

wrongExplanations.a: Premature connection webs often confuse beginners.
wrongExplanations.c: Views remain useful with or without relations.
wrongExplanations.d: Relations can be highly functional for navigation and rollups.

questions.prompt: What should a weekly review emphasize in a work Notion system?

options.text: Adding more unused dashboard widgets
What moved, what stalled, top outcomes next week, and what to archive
Renaming every property for fun
Duplicating all tasks into five identical databases

questions.explanation: Lightweight review maintains momentum and reduces false load from stale work.

wrongExplanations.a: Decorative complexity does not equal progress.
wrongExplanations.c: Cosmetic renaming is rarely high-value weekly work.
wrongExplanations.d: Duplication creates drift and double maintenance.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Collaboration, Dashboards, and Judgment
quizzes.intro: Apply maintainability, sharing, and anti-clutter judgment.

questions.prompt: What is the job of a good dashboard?

options.text: Answer "What should I do next?" quickly with views you actually use
Display every database you have ever created on one endless page
Replace the need for titles
Hide all deadlines intentionally

questions.explanation: Dashboards should reduce orientation time, not showcase unused complexity.

wrongExplanations.d: Useful dashboards surface deadlines, they do not hide them.

options.text: Because hard capture forms ensure people never forget fields under stress
Because if capture requires too much structure, people avoid capturing and the system starves
Because Notion cannot store quick notes
Because review is unnecessary if capture is perfect

questions.explanation: Reliable inputs beat perfect schemas. Sort during review, not during busy moments.

wrongExplanations.a: Heavy forms often reduce capture compliance.
wrongExplanations.c: Quick notes are a core Notion use case.
wrongExplanations.d: Review is still required to organize and prioritize.

questions.prompt: What should teams agree on when sharing a Status property?

options.text: That status values can mean anything to anyone
Clear definitions so "In progress" means the same thing across people
That status should be deleted weekly
That only emojis are allowed as statuses with no names

questions.explanation: Shared language prevents fake progress and coordination failures.

wrongExplanations.c: Deleting status weekly destroys workflow continuity.
wrongExplanations.d: Readable named statuses are clearer for most teams.

questions.prompt: Which monthly cleanup action best keeps systems healthy?

options.text: Add ten new unused properties
Archive completed work, remove ignored fields, and delete unused views
Duplicate every dashboard
Disable templates permanently

questions.explanation: Cleanup reduces noise so the remaining structure stays trustworthy.

wrongExplanations.a: More unused structure increases maintenance burden.
wrongExplanations.d: Useful templates should be refined, not discarded by default.

questions.prompt: How should Notion relate to other tools in a stack?

options.text: Notion must replace calendars, email, code hosts, and everything else
Decide which tool owns each object type and use Notion where flexible docs/databases help
Never link out to other systems
Copy every calendar event into Notion manually twice a day

questions.explanation: Mature productivity is tool pluralism with clear ownership, not forced monopoly.

wrongExplanations.a: Specialized tools often remain better for specialized jobs.
wrongExplanations.c: Links and embeds can reduce context switching when used wisely.
wrongExplanations.d: Manual double entry usually wastes time and creates drift.

questions.prompt: A beautiful dashboard has not been opened in a month. What should you conclude?

options.text: It must still be valuable because it looks impressive
Unused structure is likely clutter and should be simplified or removed
You should add more widgets immediately
Notion is broken

questions.explanation: Usage is the truth test. Decorative systems that are not opened are not helping.

wrongExplanations.a: Aesthetics without use are not productivity.
wrongExplanations.c: Adding more unused complexity worsens the problem.
wrongExplanations.d: The tool is fine; the system design needs pruning.
